headline: On October 23, 2003: Images of Eris are taken
captionCards: Eris is 27% more massive than Pluto
Eris is the largest unvisited Solar System object
instagramCaption:
Eris, a dwarf planet, is imaged for the first time. \\[Blank Line]\\ In 2003, images of Eris were captured, leading to its discovery in January 2005 by Mike Brown's team at Palomar Observatory. Eris, named after the Greco-Roman goddess of strife, is more massive than Pluto and has a high-eccentricity orbit. It remains the largest-known object in the Solar System not visited by a spacecraft. \\[Blank Line]\\ Why does this matter today? Eris' discovery challenged our understanding of the Solar System. \\[Blank Line]\\ What do you think about the ongoing exploration of our Solar System? \\[Blank Line]\\ Follow @onthisday.reels for daily history ⏳
